The only later order in the dossier that names it is EO 10450 (April 27, 1953), section 1 of which recites 'Executive Order No. 10237 of April 26, 1951'; a recital is not an end. The events that could end the application (the abolition of the Panama Canal Company and the Canal Zone agencies under the Panama Canal Act of 1979, Pub. L. 96-70, or the codified successor of Public Law 733 in title 5) are not registered in this packet. Missing sources: the Panama Canal Act of 1979 with its savings provisions, and the current text of the successor provisions of Public Law 733 in title 5, U.S. Code."]

["The order exempts Howell Cone, Collector of Customs for Customs Collection District No. 17 'for an indefinite period of time not extending beyond the appointment and qualification of his successor'. It states no calendar end, so the first end is the event that closes the exemption. No source in the packet dates that event. The same Federal Register page also prints EO 10238, a different order that is not an amendment of this one. Missing source: a dated record of when the exemption's condition was met."]

["Paragraph 5 provides: 'When the Commission deems that its work has been completed, it shall report that fact to the President, and thereupon the Commission shall cease to exist.' The end is contingent on a report. The order states no calendar end, and no held source records the Commission's completion report or the date it ceased to exist; a regex search of held order texts for the Commission's name finds only EO 10245's own copies. Missing source: the Commission's report to the President, or a Federal Register or Presidential record of its termination, with date."]

["The order (sections 1 to 8, effective July 1, 1951 under section 8) transfers the waterway and facilities, and property, records and assets, to the Panama Railroad Company, which becomes the Panama Canal Company, and revokes section 17 of Executive Order No. 1888 and Canal Zone Order No. 4. Section 4 (nothing transfers title to Canal Zone lands) and section 7 (reservation of the President's power to adjust the transfers) state no end, and the packet registers no later statute or order that ended them; the Panama Canal Act of 1979 and the treaty implementing law are not in the dossier. The machine inventory (22 clauses) lists the building lists inside section 1 and sections 2 to 4 but omits sections 5 to 8, and the own-text span runs across a Federal Register continuation page into neighboring material, so the inventory needs correction before any submission. Missing sources: the later instruments that ended sections 4 and 7, and a corrected clause inventory."]
